decisions.title: One project with two internal tracks
decisions.context: The five-member group needs one coherent Senior Project while supporting research and product responsibilities
decisions.decision: Use one title and one project plan, with Research and Innovation as coordinated internal tracks
decisions.rationale: The model, Clinical Front Door, data, contracts, evaluation, and final demonstration are interdependent
alternatives: Two separate Senior Projects
One undifferentiated workstream
consequences: One official schedule and integration gate
Both tracks share contracts and final evidence

decisions.title: Approximately 4B flagship and gated 27B stretch
decisions.context: The project needs a credible open-weight flagship target without letting scale replace architecture evidence
decisions.decision: Target approximately 4B as flagship and allow 27B only after the 4B release candidate passes every gate
decisions.rationale: Small and 4B evidence is feasible and academically stronger than premature 27B resource commitment
alternatives: Make 27B mandatory
Use only a small prototype with no flagship target
consequences: 27B is not on the critical path
Tier 4 approval and G0-G5 evidence are required before 4B training

decisions.title: Stable Model Gateway for provider replacement
decisions.context: Innovation must progress before the team model is complete without becoming coupled to an external provider
decisions.decision: Route mock, external prototype, baseline, and team model providers through one versioned Model API Contract
decisions.rationale: Provider replacement becomes a configuration and adapter change rather than a client rewrite
alternatives: Wait for the team model
Integrate each provider directly into the client
consequences: Provider-native fields remain inside adapters
Every adapter passes identical contract fixtures

decisions.title: Patient-level splitting and temporal availability
decisions.context: Medical journeys contain correlated encounters and future outcomes that can silently leak into earlier decisions
decisions.decision: Split by stable patient identity before derivation and require available_at_time for all evidence and labels
decisions.rationale: This prevents cross-split identity leakage and future-evidence inflation
alternatives: Encounter-level split
Use chart-final fields at every snapshot
consequences: Confirmed leakage invalidates affected evidence
Temporal audits are mandatory before training and evaluation

decisions.title: Supervised decision support only
decisions.context: The prototype operates in a safety-critical clinical domain without deployment-grade validation
decisions.decision: Require human confirmation and prohibit autonomous diagnosis, treatment, referral, prescribing, discharge, or care action
decisions.rationale: The academic prototype must preserve human authority and avoid unsupported clinical claims
alternatives: Patient-facing autonomous triage
Clinician-optional review
consequences: Human review is required in the API and workflow
Safety failures override average accuracy

decisions.title: Restrict non-synthetic patient data from external APIs
decisions.context: External providers may retain or process data under terms that differ from dataset and ethics authorization
decisions.decision: Default to synthetic data and require exact recorded authorization before any real, linkable, de-identified-approved, or restricted patient transfer
decisions.rationale: De-identification or dataset access alone does not authorize vendor transfer
alternatives: Allow de-identified data by default
Prohibit all external prototype providers
consequences: External adapters need payload policy tests
Missing approval blocks transfer

decisions.title: Immutable Semester 1 official schedule
decisions.context: Internal planning buffers must not overwrite faculty deadlines from the referenced activities PDF
decisions.decision: Lock the supplied Semester 1 dates in the official deadline registry and require a new official source plus human decision for correction
decisions.rationale: Official dates are external constraints while internal review dates are adjustable planning controls
alternatives: Store dates only in prose
Allow the PM agent to reschedule official dates
consequences: Verification compares the registry to canonical dates
The missing local PDF remains a visual-verification action

decisions.title: Planning-system ownership boundary
decisions.context: The GSD toolchain introduced .planning/, creating a second vocabulary for work already tracked in docs/project_management/ and project_state/. MILESTONES.md M8 and MASTER_PLAN.md Phase 6 already disagree on the 4B release-candidate window, and recording one Group Application status required editing five files by hand
decisions.decision: project_state/ and docs/ are the sole authoritative record of deadlines, milestones, tasks, risks, decisions, approvals, contracts, and specifications; .planning/ is a subordinate execution layer owning phase sequencing and per-phase artifacts only, and may reference authoritative identifiers but never hold their status, scope, or definition
decisions.rationale: Authority belongs where enforcement and ownership are. project_state/ and docs/ are covered by harness checks and JSON Schema validation while .planning/ had none, and .planning/ is a third-party format governed by the @opengsd/gsd-core release cycle rather than by this project
alternatives: Make .planning/ authoritative and reduce docs/project_management/ to generated views
Maintain both systems in parallel and synchronize by hand
Remove .planning/ and forgo the GSD phase pipeline
consequences: .planning/README.md states the boundary at the point of use
verify_harness.py enforces phase-dependency resolution, requirement-to-phase mapping, and identifier existence in project_state/
Regenerating or deleting .planning/ must never lose project state
On disagreement project_state/ and docs/ win and the .planning/ artifact is corrected
.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md is a derived index whose entries must cite a source document

decisions.title: Approximately 27B replaces approximately 4B as the flagship target
decisions.context: DEC-0002 fixed approximately 4B as the flagship and confined 27B to gated stretch scope. On 2026-08-26, while preparing the Project Idea document for the immutable DL-0002 deadline, the project owner directed that the model the project will build is approximately 27B and that the 4B target be removed entirely. Because the submitted document states the flagship scale, the record and the submission must agree
decisions.decision: Approximately 27B is the flagship target of the Research Track. The approximately 4B target is withdrawn and no longer appears as a project deliverable. All gates that DEC-0002 attached to the 4B release candidate now attach to the 27B release candidate, unchanged in substance: G0-G4 must close on recorded evidence, a valid Tier 4 manifest and explicit time-bounded human approval are required before any flagship run, and no gate may be skipped on account of the larger target
decisions.rationale: The flagship scale is the project owner's decision to make and was given directly. Recording it as a superseding decision keeps the submitted Project Idea consistent with the enforced record rather than leaving the document contradicting a locked entry
alternatives: Keep DEC-0002 and write 4B in the submitted document against the owner's instruction
Write 27B in the document and leave DEC-0002 unchanged, leaving the record self-contradictory
Treat 27B as flagship while retaining 4B as a named intermediate deliverable
consequences: RISK-0004 is restated against 27B and its probability raised to CRITICAL; compute feasibility is now the dominant threat to the Research Track flagship
The scope fallback ladder is unchanged and load-bearing: if compute cannot support stable 27B training, the delivered model is reported at its true scale and never relabelled
Small-scale architecture validation before scaling is unchanged and still gates any flagship run

docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md, docs/research/RESEARCH_SPEC.md, docs/research/SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md, docs/research/TRAINING_SPEC.md, docs/project_management/MASTER_PLAN.md, docs/project_management/MILESTONES.md and the .planning/ artifacts still name 4B and must be reconciled before the Proposal Report on 2026-10-02
Compute budget, hardware reservation, and schedule impact must be re-estimated against 27B before any Tier 3 or Tier 4 request

decisions.title: Python and FastAPI as the Clinical Front Door runtime
decisions.context: GOV-01 requires the runtime and framework choice for the Clinical Front Door to be an accepted Decision Log entry before any gateway or prototype code is written, because a material architecture choice may not be made implicitly by whoever writes the first file. No implementation code exists yet: research/, innovation/ and shared/ contain only READMEs, so the choice is still free and costs nothing to record now. The project owner selected the stack on 2026-08-30
decisions.decision: The Clinical Front Door API, the Model Gateway and the shared contract runtime are implemented in Python with FastAPI. Contract models are Pydantic models generated from or validated against the JSON Schemas already in schemas/, which remain the machine source of truth for the contracts. Provider SDKs stay inside gateway adapters, per DEC-0003
decisions.rationale: One language across the project. The Research Track is Python by necessity, scripts/ is already Python (stdlib only, deliberately), and the five shared contracts already exist as JSON Schema. Pydantic binds directly to those schemas, so the executable contract and the machine contract cannot drift into two separate definitions. Choosing a second language would mean maintaining contract models twice and keeping them in sync by hand, which is precisely the drift RISK-0006 describes
alternatives: TypeScript with Node for the Front Door API: better if the project were frontend-heavy, but introduces a second language and a second copy of the contract models, against RISK-0006
Python with Django REST Framework: heavier than needed for an API-first service with no admin or ORM requirement at this stage
Defer the choice and let it emerge from the first implementation: forbidden by GOV-01, and it is how architecture decisions become accidents
consequences: Phase 2 implementation is unblocked; contract models, the mock provider and the ten contract fixtures can now be written
shared/ holds the versioned Pydantic contract models; schemas/ remains authoritative and the models are tested against the existing fixtures in tests/fixtures/
External provider SDKs are confined to gateway adapters; no provider-specific type may appear in Front Door business logic or in a client
A dependency file and a virtual environment enter the repository for the first time. scripts/ stays stdlib-only so that verify_harness.py keeps running without installing anything
If a browser UI is later required, it consumes the same API as any other client and does not change this decision

decisions.title: Accept a non-commercial research-use ceiling on the open-weight release
decisions.context: The dataset feasibility survey of 2026-08-30 established that every candidate dataset except VQA-RAD (CC0) restricts use to non-commercial research: MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR under the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License, CheXpert under the Stanford Research Use Agreement, BraTS under a challenge data-use agreement, and CT-RATE under CC-BY-NC-SA, which additionally carries a ShareAlike term. The submitted Project Idea promises an open-weight model, a phrase normally read as weights others may freely use, including commercially. The project owner was asked whether to accept the ceiling or narrow the candidate set to protect a freer release
decisions.decision: Accept the non-commercial ceiling. The released weights are for non-commercial research use only, and the candidate set is not narrowed to avoid it. Every artifact that describes the release - the Proposal Report, the Progress Report, the model card, the repository README and any publication - states the restriction explicitly rather than using the unqualified term open-weight. The term open-weight may still be used for the property it actually denotes, that the weights are published and inspectable, but never as an implied grant of unrestricted use
decisions.rationale: This is an academic Senior Project. Its deliverable is research evidence, not a commercial artifact, so a non-commercial research licence costs the project nothing it actually needs. Narrowing the candidate set to preserve commercial rights would cost real capability: dropping the MIMIC family removes the only patient-linked multimodal cohort available, and dropping CT-RATE removes the only 3D CT source. Paying in evidence quality for a permission the project has no use for would be a bad trade
alternatives: Narrow the candidate set to permissively licensed data only: would leave VQA-RAD as effectively the sole unrestricted source, removing patient-level linkage, longitudinal structure and 3D coverage - it would gut the research contribution to protect an unused right

Leave the release terms undecided until the release itself: would let the submitted document's open-weight claim stand unqualified through the Proposal and Progress reports, which is the claim-accuracy failure the claim boundary exists to prevent

Release no weights at all and publish only code and evaluation artifacts: remains the fallback under RISK-0010 if the licence position turns out worse than assessed, but it is not warranted by the present evidence
consequences: The words describing the release change in every downstream artifact. An unqualified open-weight claim is now a known inaccuracy, not a pending detail, and TASK-0008's retrospective review must list it for correction in the Proposal Report

RISK-0010 stays OPEN and is not retired by this decision. It covers two things this decision does not settle: whether the PhysioNet licence permits releasing weights trained on MIMIC at all (TASK-0020), and whether CT-RATE's ShareAlike term propagates to the released weights

If TASK-0020 returns that PhysioNet does not permit a weights release, this decision does not authorise one anyway; the fallback in RISK-0010 applies and only cleared code and evaluation artifacts are released
If CT-RATE is used in training, the ShareAlike term must be assessed against the release licence before publication, and CT-RATE may be dropped at that point if the terms cannot be reconciled

The release licence itself is not chosen here; it is selected at the release gate once TASK-0020 and the ShareAlike assessment are resolved, and it must be at least as restrictive as the most restrictive contributing dataset

decisions.title: The literature registry is the single citation contract
decisions.context: The project maintained two independent reference lists - five entries in the submitted Project Idea and thirteen in the unsubmitted draft - with no machine-readable store and no way to tell a citation that had been checked from one written from memory. Re-verification on 2026-09-02 found a page range carried since August that no primary source confirms (LIT-0008), which a prose bibliography could not have caught.
decisions.decision: Every external factual claim in any project document cites a LIT- identifier resolving to project_state/literature.json. Formatted references are generated from citation.apa7 and never retyped. A reference may only be ACCEPTED when verification.status is VERIFIED, which requires a named primary-source method and date. A CONFLICT record may never be ACCEPTED.
decisions.rationale: The dataset feasibility survey already proved this pattern works: schema, plus a project_state registry, plus a docs page, plus a harness check. Extending it to citations makes the anti-fabrication rule machine-enforced rather than a habit, and gives LIT- identifiers the referential integrity TASK, RISK and DEC already have.
alternatives: Keep citations as prose in Markdown and rely on care at review time - rejected, because that is exactly the regime under which LIT-0008's unconfirmed page range survived five rounds of review
Adopt an external reference manager and a .bib file - rejected, because it would sit outside project_state/ and so outside DEC-0008's authority boundary and outside the harness
consequences: Reference lists in the Proposal and every later document are generated from one store
scripts/verify_harness.py gains check_literature; the harness rises from 241 to over 1100 checks
An unverified citation cannot reach a project document without failing verification
docs/academic/PROJECT_IDEA.md is not edited: it stays byte-identical to the signed PDF, and repayment lands in the Proposal
evidence: scripts/verify_citations.py - 52 of 52 identifiers re-verified online on 2026-09-02
approvers: Pending: Phurinat Polasa (owner) — this entry is proposed, not accepted; no approval has been given

decisions.title: Accept the baseline shortlist and add two comparison arms
decisions.context: BENCHMARK_CONTRACT.md names six comparison families as abstract categories with no specific model and no citation. SRCH-0006 has not yet run, so all six remain DEFERRED. Wave 1 nonetheless established that four families are internal controls the project builds rather than downloads, and that two sharp novelty threats currently have no arm that tests them.
decisions.decision: Record families 2, 3, 4 and 6 as INTERNAL_CONTROL, owing a published method precedent rather than a checkpoint. Add two comparison arms to BENCHMARK_CONTRACT.md: an LLM-orchestrated agentic planner over the same operator vocabulary, and a fixed-route-set conditional model. Leave families 1 and 5 DEFERRED until SRCH-0006 reports licence, weights and evaluation reproducibility.
decisions.rationale: Naming baselines materially changes public benchmark rules, which CLAUDE.md puts behind human approval. The two new arms exist because without them the two sharpest threats are untested: if an LLM-emitted plan matches the trained compiler at equal compute the architectural claim is dead, and if a ten-route weighting on MIMIC matches a compiled DAG the topology claim collapses to a routing claim.
alternatives: Keep the six abstract families and name nothing - rejected, because an experiment plan that cannot name its baselines is not yet an experiment plan and TASK-0009 is blocked on it
Select Mixtral as the family 5 checkpoint - rejected on evidence: it makes no equal-compute claim and at 13B active cannot be matched to a 300-700M model
Add no new arms - rejected, because it leaves the project unable to answer its two strongest challenges
consequences: BENCHMARK_CONTRACT.md gains a named baseline candidates section and two comparison arms
Family 4 (random/shuffled routing) becomes the load-bearing experiment of the project rather than a sanity check
Med-PaLM M and Med-Gemini are fixed as novelty-matrix columns and never baselines, their weights being unavailable
The compute budget rises by two arms and must be re-estimated against TASK-0018
evidence: docs/research/RELATED_WORK.md sections Novelty threats and Baseline shortlist
project_state/literature.json baseline_families[] and LIT-0024, LIT-0033, LIT-0034, LIT-0036
approvers: Pending: Phurinat Polasa (owner) — this entry is proposed, not accepted; no approval has been given

decisions.title: The Front Door target is a deployable multi-user research service
decisions.context: The Front Door has run only as a single-operator local demo: no authentication, no configuration object, no API version prefix, no error envelope, one provider thread for the whole process, and storage opt-in behind an environment variable that could not in fact be set. The owner has asked for a system that runs on a machine that is not the developer's.
decisions.decision: Target a deployable multi-user service: settings from the environment, a versioned API surface, a single error envelope, structured logging with correlation ids and redaction, token authentication tied to the human-review gate, readiness gating on the safety rules, SQLite in WAL on a volume, and one container. It remains a RESEARCH PROTOTYPE: the banner, the mandatory human confirmation and the non-deployment boundary stay, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md's exclusion of production clinical deployment is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Deployability and safety are the same requirement in two places. The human-review gate rests on reviewer_id, which is a caller-supplied string; on a network that gate is decoration. Authentication is what makes it real, so hardening is not separable from the safety claim.
alternatives: Stay a local demo — rejected: the owner asked for a usable system, and the defects found on 2026-09-02 (a broken audit sink, silently erased human reviews) were invisible precisely because nothing exercised the deployment path
Go to a full platform with Postgres, OIDC and metrics — rejected as ceremony: the append-only guarantee is implemented as SQLite triggers, and porting them buys a new failure mode and no marks
consequences: The service refuses to start unauthenticated on a non-loopback address
/ready gates traffic on the safety rule set: a Front Door without its rules must not take work
One uvicorn worker, documented — the circuit breaker is per-process
A deployment beyond loopback needs APR-0005 under the Human Approval Policy
approvers: Pending: Supreeya Nuamkhayan (owner) — this entry is proposed, not accepted

decisions.title: Re-assessment at an unchanged decision point is idempotent
decisions.context: A recommendation's identity was derived from journey and decision time alone. Re-assessing at the same instant therefore built a fresh recommendation under the same identifier with an empty review history, so a recommendation a clinician had confirmed silently reverted to unconfirmed and /recommendations/{id}/effective flipped from 200 back to 409. Nothing raised, and the database and memory disagreed afterwards.
decisions.decision: Request identity includes the snapshot checksum. An identical question already answered returns the answer already given, with its review history intact. A changed evidence set changes the checksum and is therefore a genuinely new question with a new recommendation.
decisions.rationale: The natural keys were already deterministic; they were simply incomplete. Adding the checksum makes the existing idempotency correct rather than layering an Idempotency-Key header — a second, weaker mechanism — over a broken one.
alternatives: Require an Idempotency-Key header — rejected: it adds a client obligation to work around a server-side identity bug
Refuse a duplicate assessment with 409 — rejected: re-reading a decision point is a normal clinical action, not a client error
consequences: A confirmed recommendation cannot be silently unconfirmed by a repeated request
History no longer gains duplicate entries for the same question
Recommendation identifiers change shape; nothing persists them across the change
approvers: Pending: Supreeya Nuamkhayan (owner) — this entry is proposed, not accepted

decisions.title: The evaluated care setting is adult non-trauma emergency-department first-contact triage
decisions.context: The project has never committed to a care setting. The advisor-signed Project Idea names one only in background prose ('the front door of the hospital'); its Objective, Scope and Expected Result name none. CLINICAL_WORKFLOW.md deliberately defers the question. No schema carries a care_setting field, and DEC-0001 to DEC-0015 contain no decision about setting or triage taxonomy. The cost is now measurable in three places at once: the frozen case set cannot discriminate urgency because ten of twelve cases declare the same URGENT_REVIEW floor and none declares ROUTINE_REVIEW or IMMEDIATE_REVIEW; the surveyed data is MIMIC-IV hosp and icu, an inpatient and ICU cohort, while the product is triage-shaped and its primary safety metric is under-triage; and after RISK-0013 realised, what survives of the novelty claim is a composite plus an evaluation contribution 'in a domain the field has not entered', which is empty until the domain is named.
decisions.decision: The evaluated setting is the first-contact triage station of a hospital emergency department, before physician assessment. Population: adults aged 18 or over, non-trauma, non-obstetric. Operator: a supervised triage nurse or intake staff member. Confirmer: a clinician. Arrival mode (walk-in versus ambulance) is a declared stratification variable recorded per case, not an inclusion criterion; it becomes an inclusion criterion only if a dataset survey verifies a source field for it. Two decision moments are evaluated. T0 is the earliest time at which a chief complaint and a first vital set both satisfy available_at_time <= T0; this is derivable from the journey alone and is already what REQUIRED_FRONT_DOOR_EVIDENCE encodes in innovation/gateway/safety.py. T1 is the earliest time at which at least one result-class item, a first laboratory result or a first imaging report, satisfies available_at_time <= T1, capped at T0 plus 120 minutes; a case with no result-class item by the cap is evaluated at the cap with the item recorded as not yet available and never as normal. Sixty to ninety minutes is a reporting stratum, not the definition. Every reported claim states which snapshot it was measured at. Explicitly out of scope: operating room, pre-operative assessment, anaesthesia, ICU management, ward deterioration, prehospital and field triage, consumer self-triage, paediatrics, and major trauma. The four abstract urgency levels are unchanged and no operational triage scale is adopted.
decisions.rationale: Emergency-department first-contact triage is the only candidate setting that is simultaneously implied by the signed document, already built into the machine contracts (the patient-journey event enum leads with CHIEF_COMPLAINT and TRIAGE_NOTE), already present in the twelve fixtures (chest pain, breathlessness, abdominal pain, focal neurological deficit, fever), and measured by the declared primary safety metric. The two decision moments are the substantive part: available_at_time is the project's own differentiator against the closest published work, and a single snapshot cannot exercise it. LIT-0037 (Aegle) demonstrates per-case specialist activation for clinical intake on a real cohort, but is text only, with no typed operators, no export or replay, no imaging, no compute matching and no available_at_time semantics. Naming this setting positions the project precisely where that gap is, which threat T8 requires any Front Door claim to do explicitly. Three details are deliberate. Arrival mode is a stratum rather than an inclusion criterion because no surveyed dataset has a verified arrival-mode field; asserting a walk-in cohort now would create an inclusion criterion with no source, which is the failure RELATED_WORK.md Rule 4 exists to prevent. T1 is event-anchored rather than clock-anchored because DS-0001 already records that available_at_time must derive from storetime and that a non-trivial share of rows carry charttime greater than storetime; a fixed wall-clock window would silently include or exclude results according to turnaround, about which no evidence has been recorded. Non-trauma is excluded for two reasons beyond tidiness: ACS Field Triage is the one instrument whose terms explicitly forbid incorporation into AI and machine-learning applications, and LIT-0049 supplies the only numeric under-triage target in the surveyed literature, a 5 percent goal that is trauma-specific and must not be imported into SAFETY_SPEC.md as a threshold.
alternatives: Operating room, pre-operative assessment or anaesthesia — rejected on evidence, not preference: zero candidate datasets carry peri-operative data, the patient-journey event_type enum has no PROCEDURE, SURGERY, PREOP_ASSESSMENT, INTRAOP_VITAL or PACU value, and MIMIC-IV procedures_icd is retrospective billing code that DATA_CONTRACT.md forbids as an early-snapshot input. The literature survey also never searched peri-operative work, so under RELATED_WORK.md Rule 4 its silence is NOT_REPORTED and not ABSENT — the project could not even claim the niche is open without a new search first.
ICU management or ward deterioration — rejected: occupied by NEWS2 and by LIT-0046 (Epic sepsis, emergency-department external validation), and it is not a front door.
Consumer-facing self-triage — rejected: occupied by LIT-0055, and it contradicts PRODUCT_SPEC.md, whose user is a supervised triage nurse and not a patient.
Outpatient multi-department intake — rejected: this is exactly the setting LIT-0037 (Aegle) occupies across 24 departments, which would put the project inside threat T8 rather than beside it.
Name no setting and keep deferring — rejected: it is the status quo that produced an evaluation set which cannot discriminate and a novelty claim with an undefined domain.
consequences: The claim boundary in PROJECT_CHARTER.md, 'clinical claims beyond the evaluated population and setting', gains a referent and becomes enforceable rather than a placeholder.

RISK-0014 is raised: the product setting and the surveyed data setting do not match. MIMIC-IV-ED is not a candidate dataset — it appears once in the repository, as an unexecuted search string — so CHIEF_COMPLAINT and TRIAGE_NOTE currently have no recorded data source. RISK-0002 covers modality linkage, not setting mismatch.

The frozen case set must be rebuilt to exercise all four urgency levels and to carry a T1 snapshot, and EVAL-0001 must be re-run. The escalation rate will change, and the change must be reported as a property of the case set rather than as a safety improvement.

schemas/dataset-feasibility.schema.json gains a required care_setting object and all seven existing datasets are backfilled, closing the gap that let a seven-dataset survey record no setting while DATA_CONTRACT.md mandates population, site and time period at manifest time.

The project accepts threats T5 (LIT-0036, multimodal routing on MIMIC-IV with notes and chest X-rays) and T6 (LIT-0025, Flex-MoE) rather than moving off MIMIC, because MIMIC is the only corpus supporting patient-level multimodal linkage and time-valid snapshots. This trade is stated in the Proposal rather than left implicit.

No triage taxonomy is adopted and none may be without a licence review: ESI requires written ENA permission, ACS Field Triage explicitly forbids incorporation into AI and machine-learning applications, ATS requires ACEM permission, CTAS is unresolved, MTS is licensable but no software implementation holds accreditation, and NEWS2 is freely usable but is a deterioration score rather than a triage taxonomy. KTAS, JTAS and the Thai national ED triage scale were never read (SRCH-0005 is PARTIAL).
Naming a setting is not adopting a protocol. CLINICAL_WORKFLOW.md's prohibition on mapping to a real operational triage scale without authorized clinical validation stays in force verbatim.

The comparison cohort and the committed setting are different populations. DEC-0013's fixed-route-set arm runs on MIMIC-IV hosp and icu, which is a hospital course and not a first contact. No Front Door result may be reported on that data as if it were triage-point evidence, and every results table must name its population.

The evaluated setting is committed for the contracts, product, safety screen and synthetic evaluation, all of which are under project control. Any dataset-backed claim in this setting is conditional on DS-0008 and remains a hypothesis until surveyed.

RISK-0015 is raised. Tracing the deterministic screen shows the evaluation cannot currently discriminate at all: SCR-002 raises COMPLAINT_NOT_EVALUATED_BY_RULE as UNKNOWN for every request carrying a chief complaint, and SR-002 turns any UNKNOWN flag into URGENT_REVIEW and ESCALATED, so every complaint-bearing case escalates by construction and independently of its content. The only route to IMMEDIATE_REVIEW is a TRIGGERED flag, and the only TRIGGERED flag the screen produces is missing required evidence, so the top urgency level is reachable only through absent information and never through clinical severity. Neither provider ever emits TRIGGERED. Adding ROUTINE_REVIEW cases to the frozen set therefore cannot make it discriminate; it makes the failure visible and drives escalation toward 1.0.
evidence: docs/academic/PROJECT_IDEA.md — the signed document's only setting statement, in background prose
docs/innovation/CLINICAL_WORKFLOW.md — the deliberate deferral this decision closes, and the prohibition it leaves standing
project_state/dataset_feasibility.json — DS-0001 evidence records the hosp and icu modules; no dataset records a care setting

project_state/literature.json — LIT-0037 Aegle, LIT-0036 multimodal routing, LIT-0025 Flex-MoE, LIT-0055 symptom checkers, LIT-0046 Epic sepsis; and the sole MIMIC-IV-ED mention, an unexecuted SRCH-0005 query string
docs/research/RELATED_WORK.md — threats T5, T6 and T8; the triage-taxonomy licence audit; owner decision 6
tests/fixtures/cases/ — ten of twelve cases declare an URGENT_REVIEW floor; none declares ROUTINE_REVIEW or IMMEDIATE_REVIEW
approvers: Pending: Phurinat Polasa (scope and claims) — this entry is proposed, not accepted
Pending: Thanrada Tungweerapornpong (safety) — the setting fixes what under-triage means
Recorded under APR-0002. The rationale is written so it does not depend on APR-0001's outcome, so the two may be decided in either order.

decisions.title: The Front Door is one central backend and two separate frontends: nurse intake and the central platform
decisions.context: /platform and /nurse are served from one React bundle; the surface is chosen from location.pathname and pages are hidden client-side only (innovation/workspace/src/main.tsx). Research/debug views (AgentTrace, audit history) render inside the clinical case flow, provider readiness shares a page with account settings, and the /v2/encounters route computes queue-only fields in raw SQL inside the API handler. The team cannot tell which code belongs to the nurse product and which to the platform.
decisions.decision: Keep one backend process and one versioned /v2 API. Build two frontend entry points with separate bundles from the existing Vite project: nurse.html (voice intake and handoff, role intake) and platform.html (queue, physician review, facts, audit, trace, research, readiness, settings). Shared code lives only in src/shared/. Neither app imports from the other, enforced by a test. Access is enforced by the server's role checks, never by client-side hiding.
decisions.rationale: Separate bundles make the boundary visible in the tree and in the network tab, while one package.json and one backend avoid duplicating dependencies, auth, audit and the safety screen. Server-side role checks already exist, so the split costs no new security surface.
alternatives: Two separate npm packages — rejected: identical dependencies, double maintenance for a five-person team
Keep one bundle and separate routes — rejected: this is the current state the team finds confusing
Split the Python backend into packages now — deferred: TASK-0034 and DEC-0014 own the v1/v2 gateway question
consequences: /workspace becomes a redirect to /platform
tests/test_v2.py and the Playwright entry-point test pin two HTML entries
Owners of the nurse app and the platform app must be named when this is accepted
evidence: docs/innovation/v2/baseline/ — screenshots of both surfaces before the split

decisions.title: The Innovation product family is named Pratu: Pratu Core, Pratu Intake and Pratu Console
decisions.context: The interface carried three unrelated names: 'Clinical Front Door' as the wordmark, 'JARVIS workspace' as the product line and 'Luna' as an assistant persona, plus the generic 'Nurse Intake' and 'Central Platform' after DEC-0017 split the apps. JARVIS is a third-party fictional character name, and a named persona contradicts the design system's rule against anthropomorphising the assistant.
decisions.decision: Product family Pratu (ประตู, 'door'), described as a Clinical Front Door. Pratu Core is the central backend (API, Model Gateway, deterministic safety screen, audit). Pratu Intake is the nurse app at /nurse. Pratu Console is the physician and evaluator app at /platform. The assistant is called 'ผู้ช่วยรับข้อมูล' and has no persona name. The Research model family working name is CaseGraph; a size suffix is attached only at the scale actually trained. The official academic project title is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: One name ties the three parts together and says what the product is (the entry point of care) in Thai. It removes a third-party character name and the persona. Keeping 'Clinical Front Door' as the descriptor preserves every existing document reference.
alternatives: Keep Clinical Front Door / Nurse Intake / Central Platform — rejected: generic, and JARVIS/Luna would remain
Name after a clinical role (e.g. triage) — rejected: implies the system triages, beyond the claim boundary
consequences: UI titles, wordmark and tests use Pratu Intake and Pratu Console
No trademark search has been done for 'Pratu' or 'CaseGraph'; do one before any public release
The academic title in PROJECT_IDEA.md and official submissions is unchanged; changing it needs its own approval
